mainTopic: The שליח ציבור and the ברכות of ראש השנה and יום הכיפורים: who agrees with רבן גמליאל, why, whom he exempts, and preparing one's תפילה.
overview: רבי יוחנן said two things that seem to clash: that the חכמים agree with רבן גמליאל that the שליח ציבור fulfills everyone's obligation, and that 'the הלכה follows רבן גמליאל', which implies someone still disagrees. רבי אבא's first answer, that the two statements are about different prayers, is rejected. רב נחמן בר יצחק then explains that רבי מאיר is the one who agrees, while the רבנן still argue, and a ברייתא proves this. The גמרא explains that רבי מאיר makes this exception for ראש השנה and יום הכיפורים because those ברכות are many and long, not because of their פסוקים. רב rules that saying 'ובתורתך כתוב לאמר' is enough without reciting the פסוקים, and רבי יהושע בן לוי says this holds for a יחיד and a ציבור alike. רבי אלעזר teaches that a person should arrange his תפילה before praying, and רבי אבא limits this to rare prayers; רב יהודה's practice fits because he prayed only once a month. Finally, the גמרא concludes that רבן גמליאל let the שליח ציבור exempt only field workers, who are kept away by their work, and not people in the city. The amud ends with the הדרן that completes מסכת ראש השנה.

steps.title: רבי אבא splits the two statements by type of prayer
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא explains that the חכמים agree with רבן גמליאל only for the ברכות of ראש השנה and יום הכיפורים. The 'הלכה' statement, which implies a disagreement, is about the תפילות of the rest of the year.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי אבא came back from his sea travels, he explained: The חכמים agree with רבן גמליאל about the ברכות of ראש השנה and יום הכיפורים. And 'the הלכה follows him', which shows they still argue, is about the ברכות of the whole year.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is answering an earlier question. How can רבי יוחנן say both 'the חכמים agree with רבן גמליאל' and 'the הלכה follows רבן גמליאל'? רבי אבא's answer is that each statement is about a different set of prayers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'the הלכה follows X' only makes sense if someone still disagrees with X. רבי אבא removes the clash by giving the two statements two different topics. On ראש השנה and יום הכיפורים everyone agrees, and on the rest of the year there is still a disagreement.

keyTerms.meaning: They agree; they concede
Which implies that they disagree
From the seas, meaning back from sea travels
He explained it

phrases.aramaic: כִּי סְלֵיק רַבִּי אַבָּא מִיַּמֵּי, פֵּירְשַׁהּ:
phrases.english: When Rabbi Abba came up from the sea, he explained it:
The Sages agree with Rabban Gamliel

phrases.aramaic: בִּבְרָכוֹת שֶׁל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה וְשֶׁל יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים,
phrases.english: regarding the blessings of Rosh HaShana and of Yom Kippur,
and 'the halakha is', which implies that they disagree,
phrases.notes: This points back to רבי יוחנן's other statement: 'the הלכה follows רבן גמליאל.'

phrases.english: is regarding the blessings of the whole year.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי סְלֵיק רַבִּי אַבָּא מִיַּמֵּי, פֵּירְשַׁהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the earlier contradiction between רבי יוחנן's two statements.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each statement is about different prayers.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both statements seemed to be about the same prayers, so they clashed.
steps.terutzMaskana: Everyone agrees on ראש השנה and יום הכיפורים, and there is still a disagreement about the rest of the year.

steps.title: Challenge from רבי חנה ציפוראה
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנה ציפוראה quotes רבי יוחנן saying 'the הלכה follows רבן גמליאל' about ראש השנה and יום הכיפורים. That means there is still a disagreement about those days too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so? But רבי חנה ציפוראה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: the הלכה follows רבן גמליאל regarding the ברכות of ראש השנה and יום הכיפורים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי אבא's answer. It brings a quote showing that רבי יוחנן used the word 'הלכה' about ראש השנה and יום הכיפורים themselves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבא said there is no disagreement on ראש השנה and יום הכיפורים. But if רבי יוחנן says 'the הלכה follows רבן גמליאל' on those days, someone must still disagree there. So רבי אבא's way of splitting the cases falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so? An opening word for a challenge
But didn't he say?
From the city of ציפורי

phrases.english: Is that so?! But didn't Rabbi Ḥana of Tzippori say
that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
The halakha follows Rabban Gamliel

phrases.aramaic: בִּבְרָכוֹת שֶׁל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה וְשֶׁל יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים!
phrases.english: regarding the blessings of Rosh HaShana and of Yom Kippur!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי?! וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי חָנָה צִיפּוֹרָאָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אבא's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבא's claim that everyone agrees on ראש השנה and יום הכיפורים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן used the word 'הלכה' for ראש השנה and יום הכיפורים, and that word implies an ongoing disagreement.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק splits the statements by who is speaking
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק explains that 'they agree' refers to רבי מאיר. 'The הלכה follows him, which implies a disagreement' refers to the רבנן, who still argue.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב נחמן בר יצחק said: Who is the one who agrees? רבי מאיר. And 'the הלכה', which implies a disagreement, is about the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer in place of רבי אבא's. Both statements are about ראש השנה and יום הכיפורים, but they are about different תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the split is not between prayers but between people. רבי מאיר agrees with רבן גמליאל, so 'they agree' is true about him. The רבנן still disagree, so it makes sense to say 'the הלכה follows רבן גמליאל' against them.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; this replaces the earlier answer
Who?
The Rabbis; the majority of the Sages

steps.confusionAlert: Don't get mixed up by the word 'חכמים' in 'מודים חכמים'. Here it does not mean the רבנן who argue. It means רבי מאיר, and he is the one who agrees.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: Rather, Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
Who is it that agrees? Rabbi Meir,
and 'the halakha', which implies they disagree, is about the Rabbis.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רבי אבא's answer after the challenge knocked it down.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting by people: each statement is about a different תנא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both statements were thought to be about the same group of Sages.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי מאיר agrees with רבן גמליאל, and the רבנן still argue on ראש השנה and יום הכיפורים.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows the disagreement between רבי מאיר and the Sages
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי מאיר holds the שליח ציבור fulfills everyone's obligation on ראש השנה and יום הכיפורים. The חכמים say every individual must pray for himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: For the ברכות of ראש השנה and יום הכיפורים, the שליח ציבור fulfills the obligation for the many. These are the words of רבי מאיר. The חכמים say: just as the שליח ציבור is obligated, so every single individual is obligated.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove רב נחמן בר יצחק's answer. It shows that רבי מאיר and the חכמים really do disagree about ראש השנה and יום הכיפורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר's view matches רבן גמליאל's, so he is the one who 'agrees'. The חכמים require each person to pray on his own, so they are the ones still arguing. That is why 'the הלכה follows רבן גמליאל' makes sense even on these days.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
The prayer leader who prays on behalf of the congregation
Fulfills their obligation for them
An individual

steps.whatToRemember: In the final answer, רבי מאיר agrees with רבן גמליאל that on ראש השנה and יום הכיפורים the שליח ציבור fulfills everyone's obligation. The חכמים disagree, and רבי יוחנן rules like רבן גמליאל.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets out the practical rule: on ראש השנה and יום הכיפורים, the שליח ציבור's repetition can fulfill the obligation for someone who cannot pray on his own.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: בְּרָכוֹת שֶׁל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה וְשֶׁל יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים —
phrases.english: As it is taught: The blessings of Rosh HaShana and of Yom Kippur:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלִיחַ צִבּוּר מוֹצִיא הָרַבִּים יְדֵי חוֹבָתָן,
phrases.english: the prayer leader fulfills the obligation of the many,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
And the Sages say:
Just as the prayer leader is obligated,
so too each and every individual is obligated.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source that supports רב נחמן בר יצחק's answer.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי מאיר agrees with רבן גמליאל and the רבנן disagree, about ראש השנה and יום הכיפורים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recording the disagreement between רבי מאיר and the חכמים.

steps.title: What makes these days different?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי מאיר agrees with רבן גמליאל only for the ברכות of ראש השנה and יום הכיפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about these ברכות?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question that sets up the next few moves. It wants to know why רבי מאיר says the שליח ציבור covers everyone only on ראש השנה and יום הכיפורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 showed that רבי מאיר makes the שליח ציבור cover everyone only on these two days. The גמרא now wants the reason. Something about these ברכות must make them harder for an individual to say.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? It asks for the reason behind a distinction.
These, meaning these ones.

phrases.english: What is different about these?
phrases.notes: 'These' are the ברכות of ראש השנה and יום הכיפורים, where רבי מאיר agrees the שליח ציבור covers everyone.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא הָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind רבי מאיר's position, which the ברייתא in step 4 proved.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי מאיר limits the שליח ציבור's power to cover everyone to the ברכות of ראש השנה and יום הכיפורים.

steps.title: The many verses cannot be the reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the reason is the many פסוקים in these ברכות, then rejects this using רב's ruling that saying 'ובתורתך כתוב לאמר' is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might say it is because there are many פסוקים. But רב חננאל said in the name of רב that once a person says 'And in Your Torah it is written, saying,' he no longer needs to say the פסוקים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible answer: these ברכות are hard because they contain many פסוקים. It immediately knocks this answer down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מלכיות, זכרונות and שופרות each normally include a set of פסוקים. רב rules that a person who says the line 'ובתורתך כתוב לאמר' does not have to recite those פסוקים. If the פסוקים can be left out, they cannot be what makes these ברכות too hard for an individual.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say. It introduces a suggestion that is usually about to be rejected.
The פסוקים are many.
'And in Your Torah it is written, saying.' This is the line in the תפילה that introduces the פסוקים.
He no longer needs to.

phrases.english: If you say it is because the verses are many,
but didn't Rav Chananel say that Rav said:
once he has said 'And in Your Torah it is written, saying,'
he no longer needs to!
phrases.notes: He no longer needs to say the פסוקים themselves.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא מִשּׁוּם דִּנְפִישִׁי קְרָאֵי וְהָאָמַר רַב חֲנַנְאֵל אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes an answer to step 5's question and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the suggestion that the many פסוקים are the reason for רבי מאיר's distinction.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: According to רב, the פסוקים do not have to be said at all, so they cannot be what makes these ברכות hard for an individual.

steps.title: Because there are many blessings
steps.stepSummary: The real reason is that these ברכות are many and long.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is because the ברכות are many.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its real answer. These days have many long ברכות, so not everyone can say them properly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra ברכות of ראש השנה and יום הכיפורים are long and unusual. Many people cannot handle them on their own, so רבי מאיר lets the שליח ציבור cover them. This is not needed for the regular, familiar תפילות of the year.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It introduces the accepted answer after a rejected one.
The ברכות are many or lengthy.

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר's distinction depends on how long and how many the ראש השנה and יום הכיפורים ברכות are, not on the פסוקים inside them.

phrases.english: Rather, it is because the blessings are many.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מִשּׁוּם דְּאָוְושִׁי בְּרָכוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer rejected in step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: These days have many long ברכות, which are hard for an individual, so the שליח ציבור covers everyone.

steps.title: Looking again at רב's ruling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to רב חננאל's statement in the name of רב in order to study it on its own.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now for the statement itself. רב חננאל said in the name of רב: once a person says 'And in Your Torah it is written, saying,' he no longer needs to say the פסוקים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the ruling it quoted in step 6 so it can look at it on its own. This step sets up a question about how far the ruling reaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now, רב's ruling was only a tool for rejecting a suggestion. Now the ruling itself becomes the topic. The next question will be who exactly the ruling applies to.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter itself. The גמרא is returning to study a statement that it quoted earlier only in passing.

phrases.aramaic: גּוּפָא, אָמַר רַב חֲנַנְאֵל אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: The matter itself: Rav Chananel said that Rav said:
once he has said 'And in Your Torah it is written, saying,'
he no longer needs to.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא אָמַר רַב חֲנַנְאֵל אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings back the ruling quoted in step 6 for its own discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Saying 'ובתורתך כתוב לאמר' is enough, and the פסוקים themselves do not need to be recited.

steps.title: Some thought it was only for an individual
steps.stepSummary: Some people concluded that רב's ruling applies only to someone praying alone, not to a ציבור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some understood from this that the rule applies only to an individual, but not to a ציבור.
steps.whatsHappening: Some people drew a limit from רב's ruling. They thought the shortcut works only for a יחיד, while a ציבור must still say the פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא does not say why they limited the rule. It is only an assumption that some people made, and the next step rejects it.

keyTerms.meaning: They understood from it. It introduces an assumption that often gets corrected.
These words apply only. It sets a limit on a ruling.
An individual or a congregation.

phrases.english: They understood from it: this applies only to an individual,
but to a congregation, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: סְבוּר מִינַּהּ הָנֵי מִילֵּי בְּיָחִיד אֲבָל בְּצִבּוּר לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes a limit on the scope of רב's ruling from step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A suggested reading: the shortcut applies only to a יחיד.

steps.title: It applies to an individual and a congregation alike
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי rules that the shortcut works both for a יחיד and for a ציבור.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was said: רבי יהושע בן לוי said, both for an individual and for a ציבור, once a person says 'And in Your Torah it is written, saying,' he no longer needs to say the פסוקים.
steps.whatsHappening: A statement of רבי יהושע בן לוי is brought to reject the limit from step 9. The shortcut works for everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 assumed that a ציבור must still say the פסוקים. רבי יהושע בן לוי says clearly that there is no difference. Saying 'ובתורתך כתוב לאמר' is enough in both cases.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated. It introduces a teaching of an אמורא.
Both an individual and a congregation, alike.

steps.whatToRemember: Saying 'ובתורתך כתוב לאמר' frees anyone, whether a יחיד or a ציבור, from reciting the פסוקים.

phrases.aramaic: אִתְּמַר, אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי:
phrases.english: It was stated: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
both an individual and a congregation,
once he has said 'And in Your Torah it is written, saying,'
he no longer needs to.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִתְּמַר אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי אֶחָד יָחִיד אֶחָד צִבּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the limit to a יחיד that was proposed in step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the assumption that a ציבור must still recite the פסוקים.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי יהושע בן לוי says outright that the rule is the same for a יחיד and a ציבור.

steps.title: Arrange your prayer before you pray
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר teaches that a person should always arrange his תפילה first and only then pray.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: a person should always arrange his תפילה and afterward pray.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins. רבי אלעזר says that a person should get his תפילה in order before he starts to pray.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This connects to the topic of long, unfamiliar ברכות. Preparing ahead helps a person say the תפילה correctly. רבי אלעזר states it as a general rule, using the word 'always.'

keyTerms.meaning: Always.
He should arrange or set in order.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
a person should always arrange his prayer,
and afterward pray.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר לְעוֹלָם יַסְדִּיר אָדָם תְּפִלָּתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new related topic about getting ready before praying.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person should arrange his תפילה before he prays.

steps.title: רבי אבא limits it to rare prayers
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא says that רבי אלעזר's rule makes sense for ראש השנה, יום הכיפורים and other prayers said only now and then, but not for the daily prayers of the year.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said: רבי אלעזר's statement makes sense for the ברכות of ראש השנה, יום הכיפורים and occasional prayers, but not for the prayers of the whole year.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא narrows רבי אלעזר's rule. Arranging the תפילה ahead of time is needed only for prayers that a person does not say often.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Daily prayers are familiar, so a person does not need to prepare them. Rare prayers are unfamiliar, so preparing makes sense. This changes the 'always' of step 11 into a limited rule.

keyTerms.meaning: It is reasonable or makes sense.
His statement.
Occasions that come only at intervals, meaning prayers said only now and then.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said:
Rabbi Elazar's statement makes sense
for the blessings of Rosh HaShanah
and of Yom Kippur and of occasional times,
phrases.notes: 'פרקים' means prayers that come only once in a while, so they are not familiar.

phrases.english: but for those of the whole year, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא מִסְתַּבְּרָא מִילְּתֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the scope of רבי אלעזר's rule from step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Arranging one's תפילה beforehand is needed only for rare prayers, not for the daily ones.

steps.title: But רב יהודה arranged even his regular prayers
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי אבא: רב יהודה arranged his תפילה before praying even on ordinary days.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But רב יהודה would arrange his תפילה and then pray!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אבא's limit by pointing to the practice of רב יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבא said that preparing is not needed for regular prayers. Yet רב יהודה prepared even his regular prayers. That seems to show that preparing applies all year.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so? It introduces a challenge.
He would arrange his prayer.

phrases.english: Is that so?!

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא רַב יְהוּדָה מְסַדַּר צְלוֹתֵיהּ וּמְצַלֵּי!
phrases.english: But Rav Yehudah would arrange his prayer and then pray!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי וְהָא רַב יְהוּדָה מְסַדַּר צְלוֹתֵיהּ וּמְצַלֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אבא's limit from step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבא's claim that regular prayers do not need to be arranged beforehand.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב יהודה arranged his regular prayers too, which suggests that preparing applies all year.

steps.title: רב יהודה prayed only once a month
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה is different. He prayed only once every thirty days, so for him every prayer counted as a rare one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה is different. Since he prayed only once every thirty days, for him it was like occasional prayers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. רב יהודה's case fits רבי אבא's rule, because for him even regular prayers were rare.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה prayed only once a month, so his prayers were not familiar to him. That puts him in the category of פרקים. רבי אבא's limit stays in place.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different. It marks a special case.
Thirty days.
It is similar or counts as.

steps.whatToRemember: Preparing one's תפילה depends on how familiar it is: it is needed for rare prayers, and anyone who prays rarely is treated like that too.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean that רב יהודה's custom is the normal practice. His case was special because he prayed so rarely, and the general rule for daily prayers does not change.

phrases.english: Rav Yehudah is different,
since from thirty days to thirty days
he would pray,
it is like occasional times.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי רַב יְהוּדָה כֵּיוָן דְּמִתְּלָתִין יוֹמִין לִתְלָתִין יוֹמִין הֲוָה מְצַלֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 13's challenge and keeps רבי אבא's limit.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: רב יהודה's situation is unusual.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב יהודה's custom shows that preparing applies even to regular prayers.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because רב יהודה prayed only once every thirty days, his prayers counted as פרקים, so רבי אבא's rule stands.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל exempted even the people in the fields
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר עוירא, quoting רבי שמעון חסידא, reports that רבן גמליאל let the שליח ציבור exempt even the people working out in the fields.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר עוירא said in the name of רבי שמעון חסידא: רבן גמליאל would exempt even the people in the fields.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a report about how far רבן גמליאל's rule reaches. According to this report, the שליח ציבור's prayer covered even people who were far away in the fields.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן גמליאל holds that the שליח ציבור can fulfill the obligation for people who did not pray themselves. This statement adds that the rule reached even people who were away from the בית כנסת, out in the fields. The word 'even' will become important in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Exempts, covers someone's obligation
The תנא who holds that the שליח ציבור's prayer covers the people listening
The people who are out in the fields
Even

phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Avira said
that Rabbi Shimon Chasida said:
Rabban Gamliel would exempt
even the people who are in the fields.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר עַוִּירָא אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן חֲסִידָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: who is covered by the שליח ציבור under רבן גמליאל's view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Under רבן גמליאל's view, the שליח ציבור exempts even the people in the fields.

steps.title: So surely the people in the city are covered too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the word 'even' to mean that people here in the city are certainly covered as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it goes without saying that those who are here are covered!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws out what the word 'even' seems to imply: if the far-away field workers are covered, the people in the city surely are. This step sets up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'even X' usually means X is the hardest case, so easier cases are included automatically. The גמרא assumes the people in the city are the easier case. The next step will question that assumption.

keyTerms.meaning: And it goes without saying
Who are standing here, in the city

phrases.english: And it goes without saying
about those who are standing here?!
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the people in the city who did not come to the בית כנסת.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא מִיבַּעְיָא הָנֵי דְּקָיְימִי הָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an implication from the word 'even' in step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does 'even the fields' mean the people in the city are covered all the more?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The גמרא assumes yes for now, and the next step challenges this.

steps.title: On the contrary: the field workers have an excuse, the city people do not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues the opposite: the people in the fields are held back by their work, while the people in the city have no such excuse.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary! These people (in the fields) are held back by forces beyond their control. Those people (in the city) are not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the assumption from step 16. It argues that the field workers are actually the easier case to cover, not the harder one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The field workers could not come because of their work. The city people could have come and chose not to. So the city people deserve less help from the שליח ציבור, and the 'all the more' reasoning runs backward.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary, the opposite makes more sense
They are held back by circumstances beyond their control (אונס)

steps.confusionAlert: The two 'הָנֵי' refer to different groups. The first one is the people in the fields, who are held back. The second one is the people in the city, who are not.

phrases.english: On the contrary: these are held back by forces beyond their control,
phrases.notes: 'These' are the people in the fields, kept away by their work.

phrases.english: those are not held back by forces beyond their control.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַדְּרַבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the 'all the more' reasoning of step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of step 15 that the city people are covered all the more.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Being held back by circumstances (אונס) is what earns the exemption. The field workers have it and the city people do not, so the city people should not be included automatically.

steps.title: Support: people behind the כהנים are left out of the blessing
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא taught by אבא, son of רב בנימין בר חייא, rules that people standing behind the כהנים are not included in ברכת כהנים, which shows that people who could have made the effort lose out.
steps.simpleTranslation: As אבא, son of רב בנימין בר חייא, taught: people standing behind the כהנים are not included in the blessing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up the אדרבה argument. It shows that a person who could have put himself in the right place, and did not, is left out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The people behind the כהנים could easily have moved to the front, so they lose the ברכה. By the same logic, people who are truly held back are included. This matches the claim that the field workers are covered and the city people are not.

keyTerms.meaning: As was taught (in a ברייתא)
Behind the כהנים during ברכת כהנים
Included in the blessing

phrases.english: As Abba, the son
of Rav Binyamin bar Chiyya, taught:
people who are behind the kohanim —
are not included in the blessing.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתָנֵי אַבָּא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב בִּנְיָמִין בַּר חִיָּיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the אדרבה challenge in step 17.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that people who are not held back lose out, while people who are held back are included.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of אבא, son of רב בנימין בר חייא, about people standing behind the כהנים.

steps.title: Corrected report: only the people in the fields were exempted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the first report and brings רבין's version: רבן גמליאל exempted only the people in the fields, because their work holds them back, and not the people in the city.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, when רבין came, he said in the name of רבי יעקב בר אידי, who said in the name of רבי שמעון חסידא: רבן גמליאל exempted only the people in the fields. What is the reason? Because they are held back by their work. But in the city, he did not exempt them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the challenge and replaces the first report with a different one. In the new version, רבן גמליאל exempted only the field workers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אֶלָּא' shows that the first version of רבי שמעון חסידא's statement is being dropped. The new version gives the reason openly: the field workers are held back by their work. That reason does not apply to the people in the city, so they are not covered.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (dropping what was said before)
When רבין came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)
What is the reason?
By their work

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבן גמליאל, the שליח ציבור exempts only people who are truly held back, like workers in the fields. People in the city who could have come are not exempted.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that being held back (אונס) is the key reason for the exemption. It is not just about distance.

phrases.english: Rather, when Ravin came:
Rabbi Yaakov bar Idi said
that Rabbi Shimon Chasida said:
Rabban Gamliel did not exempt
anyone except the people in the fields.
What is the reason?
Because they are held back by their work.
But in the city — no.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, כִּי אֲתָא רָבִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge of steps 17-18 and replaces the report from step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replacing the first report with a corrected version of the same statement.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבן גמליאל exempted even the people in the fields, and the city people all the more.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבן גמליאל exempted only the people in the fields, because their work holds them back. The people in the city are not exempted.

steps.title: Hadran: Closing פרק יום טוב and Finishing מסכת ראש השנה
steps.stepSummary: The traditional closing line, saying 'we will return to you' to the פרק יום טוב and marking the end of מסכת ראש השנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק יום טוב, and מסכת ראש השנה is finished.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is not making a new point here. This is the standard הדרן line that closes the last פרק and the whole מסכת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The discussion about רבן גמליאל and the שליח ציבור (steps 15-19) was the last argument in the מסכת. This line simply marks the finish. 'הדרן עלך' is a promise that we will come back and learn this פרק again.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you. This is the closing formula said at the end of a פרק or מסכת.
The name of this פרק, taken from its opening words about ראש השנה falling on שבת.
It is finished or completed.
A tractate, meaning one whole book of the גמרא.

steps.whatToRemember: מסכת ראש השנה ends with the ruling from steps 15-19: the שליח ציבור's תפילה exempts only people who are kept away by their work, like field workers, and not people who could easily have come and prayed.

phrases.english: We will return to you, [chapter] Yom Tov
and Tractate Rosh Hashanah is completed

steps.triggerLanguage: הַדְרָן עֲלָךְ יוֹם טוֹב וּסְלִיקָא לַהּ מַסֶּכֶת רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Formally closes the פרק and the מסכת after the final ruling in step 19.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: פרק יום טוב is closed and מסכת ראש השנה is complete. The final ruling left standing is רבין's version: רבן גמליאל exempted only those kept away by their work.
